notes: §1985:VI.6.6.4 GR5 puts ADD under the common paragraphs: "Additional rules and explanations relative to this statement are given under the appropriate paragraphs" (Scope of Statements, ROUNDED, ON SIZE ERROR, The Arithmetic Statements, Overlapping Operands, Multiple Results, CORRESPONDING). BindAdd binds formats 1 and 2 and hands format 3 to BindAddCorresponding. The 1985 arms are two: a bare ROUNDED is the one 1985 rounding through RoundingOf, with ROUNDED MODE IS refused at 85 by VisitRoundedPhrase (COBOL0803), and CheckComposite caps the composite at the edition's 18 digits, over every operand in format 1 and without the GIVING items in format 2. EmitInPlace and EmitGiving form the sum once (Snapshot when there are several receivers) and store left to right (§1985:VI.6.4.6: "considered to be written in the same left-to-right sequence that the multiple results are specified"); EmitArith, GuardedStore and StoreArith (CobolNum.TryStore) keep a size-error receiver unchanged, store the rest and run the size-error phrase once after every store, which CorrespondingEmitter.Emit shares pair by pair; with no phrase the store is unchecked and execution goes on. Overlapping operands are undefined in 1985, so nothing is owed there; VisitStatementBlock refuses (COBOL2796) an ADD with a size-error phrase and no END-ADD where an imperative-statement is printed. Probed at --std 85: the standard's own ADD A, B, C, TO C, D (C), E with ones gives C 4, D (4) 13, E 13; 1149 ROUNDED into S99PP gives 1100 and 1251 gives 1300; -1.25 ROUNDED into S9V9 gives -1.3; GIVING a ROUNDED edited item and an unrounded item gives 6.3 and 6.2 from 6.26; ADD CORR skips FILLER, a pair with a non-numeric member and an OCCURS entry, leaves the overflowing pair unchanged and runs ON SIZE ERROR after the later pair is stored; END-ADD closes an ADD inside IF; NOT ON SIZE ERROR alone is skipped on a size error and execution continues; a 20-digit format 1 composite and a 19-digit format 2 composite are refused (COBOL0805) while a 9(18) operand GIVING a V99 item compiles; two operands after TO with GIVING are refused (COBOL1689). The witness runs ROUNDED on one receiver (11.25 into 99V9 gives 11.3) and ON SIZE ERROR leaving a PIC 9 receiver at 9.

next.reason: 1985 subjects ADD to 'Overlapping Operands', under which shared storage not from the same entry makes 'the result of the execution of such a statement is undefined' (§1985:VI.6.4.5). 2023's list (§2023:14.9.2.4 GR6 'Additional rules and explanations relative to this statement are given in 14.6.13.2, Incompatible data; ... 14.7.7, Arithmetic statements') drops that reference, and §2023:14.7.7 GR4 specifies an intermediate data item ('The initial evaluation of the statement is done and the result of this operation is placed in an intermediate data item'), so 'the results contained in the receiving operands for all arithmetic statements are defined regardless of whether any of the sending operands share storage' (§2023:14.7.7). An ADD with overlapping operands goes from undefined to defined; 14.6.10 applies only where the statement's rules give no specific result. Incompatible data (EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE) is newly referenced.
